messages:
marcus: quick thought — instead of full hot-standby GPUs, what if runtime wrote a tiny local snapshot of KV/prefix state on preempt signal and pushed it to a regional object store. on resume a different pool can pull the snapshot and re-attach the kv cache. avoids model warmup for most requests and keeps token continuity.

devon: hmm, how tiny are we talking? what do we persist exactly?

marcus: just the live KV pages + last-request checkpoints (sequence id, client stream offset, stream checksum). typically a few MB per active session for our short-session workloads.

anya: curious about in-flight streaming. if we flush local cache then the stream needs to cutover gracefully — do we requeue or splice?

marcus: two pieces: 1) emit a short-lived cutover token header to clients before we ack preempt, so clients keep sending to proxy with header `X-CUTOVER-TOKEN: <id>`. 2) proxy/backoff service will try to attach the snapshot and resume; if resume fails we return a short retry directive to client to reconnect with exponential backoff.

devon: can you sketch the client flow?

marcus: pseudo: ```
client.open_stream()
server.on_preempt() -> server.write_snapshot(path) -> server.push_to_store(path) -> server.send_header('X-CUTOVER-TOKEN', id)
client.continue_stream(header=id) -> proxy.lookup_snapshot(id) -> proxy.attach_kv(snapshot) -> new_worker.pull(snapshot) -> resume
```

kai: sounds promising. need to be careful about races: snapshot might be stale or partial. how do we detect corruption?

marcus: snapshot includes a small manifest + checksum and an atomic marker file on store. we only accept snapshots with complete marker. if incomplete, fallback to requeue/restart.

riley: storage/egress cost? pushing snapshots on every preempt could blow margins for high-churn clusters.

marcus: agreed — plan is: only snapshot sessions above threshold (e.g., >10s active or >N tokens). cheap sessions skip snapshot and use our existing short-retry requeue. also use regional cheap object store (minio in same AZ) to avoid cross-region egress.

anya: security: snapshots contain KV that might have user PII. must be encrypted at rest and in transit. we should use KMS and per-tenant envelope keys.

marcus: yes — encrypt with customer/cluster KMS key before pushing. metadata in manifest is minimal and encrypted as well.

devon: what about latency of resume? pulling snapshot + attach could add 150-500ms depending on IO; still way better than full model cold-start for many use-cases. we should benchmark.

kai: metrics to track: resume_success_rate, median_resume_ms, cost_per_resume_usd, lost_tokens_count, percentage_sessions_snapshotting.

instance-evict-bot: NOTICE: instance i-08f... in us-west-2a scheduled for termination in 120s (spot reclaim).

marcus: that eviction just triggered the idea. thinking runtime reacts to termination-notice by prioritizing snapshot + marker write, then push.

devon: i'll spike a PoC: local snapshotter + minio uploader, branch `evict-snap-poc`. will try with a small benchmark harness.

anya: can we run a canary on a mixed pool (spot + ondemand) with lower qps and measure resume latencies + cost delta?

devon: yes, will set up a canary job and a dashboard. estimate cost model: snapshot push adds ~0.02 USD per resume (bandwidth + storage ops) but saves ~0.5-1.5 USD in avoided warm GPU minutes for heavy sessions — preliminary numbers.

riley: add KMS config and retention policies to the PoC so security sign-off is faster.

marcus: agreed. devon, tag me and kai on the PR. we'll demo at infra sync next week. :+1:
